html:
The Sultanate of Mogadishu was a Muslim trading city on the Somali coast of the Indian Ocean that flourished from about the 10th to the 16th century.

Settled by Somali and Arab and Persian merchants, it traded gold from the south, ivory and its own woven cloth, which was sold as far as Egypt. It minted its own coins and built mosques such as the mosque of Fakr ad-Din of 1269.

Ibn Battuta, who visited in 1331, described a large and rich city and its sultan's court. It later fell under the Ajuran and declined as the Portuguese disrupted the trade. Mogadishu remained the main city of the south and became the capital of independent Somalia.
sum: The Sultanate of Mogadishu was a Muslim trading city on the Somali coast of the Indian Ocean that flourished from about the 10th to the 16th century.
